html:
In 1460 the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II conquered the Despotate of the Morea in the Peloponnese, the last Byzantine land in Greece.

Since the revolt of 1453 and 1454 the despots Thomas and Demetrios Palaiologos had paid tribute to the sultan, but they fought each other and fell behind on payments. Mehmed marched south in 1458 and took part of the land. In 1460 he came back to finish the job.

Demetrios surrendered Mistra at the end of May 1460, and was given land in Thrace. Thomas fled to Italy and gave the pope the head of Saint Andrew as a gift. A few castles held out into 1461, and the Venetian ports stayed Venetian for decades. The next year Trebizond fell too, ending the last Byzantine state anywhere. Thomas's son Andreas later sold his claim to the throne of Byzantium to the kings of France and Spain.
sum: In 1460 the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II conquered the Despotate of the Morea in the Peloponnese, the last Byzantine land in Greece.
